新闻报道1.
News Report 1.
一名女子被指控违反罗德岛州法律禁止喂养野生动物。
A woman was charged with allegedly violating a Rhode Island city law against feeding wild animals.
这位 55 岁妇女的邻居指责她导致该地区的鼠患问题更加严重。
The 55-year-old woman's neighbours blame her for making the area's rat problem worse.
新安装的摄像头捕捉到了几只活跃在中午时分。
Newly installed cameras captured several rats active in the middle of the day.
邻居们说，夜晚。
Neighbours say that it's even worse during the night.
这名女子和她的父母回家后，她告诉记者，她被指控喂鸟。
The woman and her parents, who own the home, told reporters that she's being charged for feeding birds.
谁会知道仅仅爱护动物就能“你这么麻烦，”她说。
Who would have known just loving animals gets you that much trouble, she said.
禁止喂食任何野生动物，包括鸟类，位于罗德岛市。
It is prohibited to feed any wild animals, including birds, in Rhode Island City.
尽管如此，尽管该女子的本意是喂鸟类，很明显老鼠也受益。
Nevertheless, while the woman's intention was to feed birds, it is clear that rats were also benefiting.
市政管理局局长安东尼·莫雷蒂表示他在附近看到了20多只老鼠女人的家。
Antony Moretti, Director of the City Administration, said he saw more than 20 rats near the woman's home.
他说需要几个月的时间才能问题得到控制。
He said it will take months to get the problem under control.
新闻报道2.
News report 2.
为了准备最终将宇航员送上火星，美国宇航局周五开始接受四人申请在火星沙丘生活一年阿尔法。
To prepare for eventually sending astronauts to Mars, NASA began taking applications Friday for four people to live for a year in Mars Dune Alpha.
这是一个占地 1,700 平方英尺的火星栖息地休斯顿的一栋建筑内。
That's a 1,700-square-foot Martian habitat inside a building in Houston.
有偿志愿者将在类似于火星。
The paid volunteers will work in an environment similar to Mars.
他们与家人的交流将受到限制，食物和资源。
They will have limited communications with family, restricted food and resources.
美国宇航局计划进行三项实验，其中第一项一期将于明年秋季开始。
NASA is planning three experiments with the first one starting in the fall next year.
食物将全部在太空中即食食物。
Food will all be ready to eat space food.
有些植物可以生长，但土豆不行就像电影《火星救援》一样。
Some plants will be grown, but not potatoes like in the movie The Martian.
我们想了解人类在他们。
We want to understand how humans perform in them.
首席科学家格蕾丝·道格拉斯说道。
Said Lead Scientist Grace Douglas.
我们正在观察火星的现实情况。
We're looking at Mars' realistic situations.
申请程序已于周五开放，但他们没有寻找任何人。
The application process opened Friday and they're not seeking just anybody.
要求很严格，包括硕士学位在科学、工程或数学领域或飞行员经验。
The requirements are strict, including a master's degree in a science, engineering or math field or pilot experience.
仅限美国公民或美国永久居民是可以接受的。
Only American citizens or permanent U.S. residents are acceptable.
申请人年龄必须在 30 至 55 岁之间，并且身体健康。
Applicants must be between 30 and 55 and in good physical health.
前加拿大宇航员克里斯说，态度是关键哈德菲尔德。
Attitude is key, said former Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield.
他说，参与者需要超级有能力、足智多谋、不依赖他人感觉舒服。
He said the participants need to be super competent, resourceful and not rely on other people to feel comfortable.
日本市长周四为咬伤垒球运动员的奥运金牌。
A Japanese mayor apologized Thursday for biting the Olympic gold medal of a softball player.
名古屋市长河村隆史称赞运动员美绪在公共媒体活动期间转至。
Nagoya Mayor Takashi Kawamura had praised athlete Mio Goto during a public media event.
他让她把奖章放在他的脖子。
He asked her to put the medal around his neck.
然后，川村咬了一口。
Kawamura then bit into it.
在记者面前咬奖牌，摄影师已经成为奥运会的常见姿势奖牌获得者。
Biting a medal in front of journalists and photographers has become a common pose for Olympic medalists.
然而，这只对获胜者自己来说，不是别人。
However, it is only for the winners themselves, not others.
真的很抱歉伤害了宝物” 川村周四对记者说。
I'm really sorry that I hurt the treasure of the gold medalist, Kawamura told reporters Thursday.
市长表示，奖章完好无损，他愿意支付一个新的。
The mayor said the medal was undamaged, though he offered to pay for the cost of a new one.
然而，后藤已经接受了国际奥委会的据日本媒体报道，報告。
Goto, however, has accepted the International Olympic Committee's offer of a replacement, according to Japanese media reports.
电视上播出的这一幕引起了成千上万的向市政厅投诉。
The scene broadcast on television prompted thousands of complaints to City Hall.
一些奥运选手表示，他们把奖牌视为宝藏，这是不尊重和不可接受的让川村咬一个。
Some Olympians said they treat their medals as treasures and that it was disrespectful and unacceptable for Kawamura to bite one.
如果这种事发生在我身上，我一定会哭的。另一名运动员 Naohisa Takato 说道。
I would cry if that happened to me, said another athlete, Naohisa Takato.
我如此温柔地对待自己的金牌我不会抓挠它。
I handle my own gold medal so gently that I would not scratch it.
